preamble: Fronting of the voiced velar stop [ɡ] to the voiced palatal stop [ɟ] next to front vowels. It is a productive allophonic rule in Turkish native vocabulary and in Modern Greek, and it appears historically in Albanian, where Latin g before front vowels is reflected by gj [ɟ] in loanwords such as engjëll 'angel'.

examples.from: /ɡ/ next to front vowels, e.g. gel 'come!'
examples.note: In native Turkic words the velars /k, ɡ/ are palatalized to [c, ɟ] when adjacent to the front vowels /e, i, œ, y/; the spelling does not mark the alternation.
Greek has palatals [c, ɟ, ç, ʝ] as allophones of the velars /k, ɡ, x, ɣ/ before the front vowels /e, i/.
Borrowed through Vulgar Latin; the Albanian letter gj is the voiced palatal plosive [ɟ].
